scope: Interpretation of pinned provider-capability and CodeQL security-query table facts; not adoption, target behavior, rendered-page assurance, or whole-artifact omission certification.

propositions.statement: The provider support page distinguishes provider-specific regex patterns, generic regex patterns, and AI-detected secrets. These categories must not be flattened into a universal capability promise.

The category table presents user alerts for all categories; partner notifications apply to participating providers, default push protection to most provider patterns, and configurable protection to generic and some provider patterns.
Generic patterns do not support validity checks. The generic pattern precision labels are estimates of typical false-positive rates, not guarantees.
The generic EC key row appears on GHES above 3.18 and the generic PRIVATE KEY row above 3.19. A snapshot row is not an all-version capability assertion.
Password detection uses an AI feature gate; the page explicitly denies push protection and validity checks for passwords.

Partner validity checks require the stated Team or Enterprise feature enablement; extended metadata follows a separate gate. Pinned gates list partner validity for GHES >=3.20, and extended metadata for GHES >=3.23; FPT/GHEC have wildcard entries.
Push protection supports recent token versions confidently identifiable by the service. A provider capability flag does not promise blocking of every legacy token version.
The pinned middleware chooses separate fpt, ghec, or ghes-currentRelease YAML data and declines an unknown enterprise-server version. Cross-version matrix families must retain their source paths.

hasValidityCheck and hasExtendedMetadata can be Liquid expressions. The middleware evaluates those string expressions in request context before parsing the result as YAML. Literal source fidelity does not prove the effective rendered boolean for a target.

The UI labels isPublic as Partner and isPrivateWithGhas as User alert. Legacy claim labels public-support/private-with-Advanced-Security describe raw key names; they need this contextual glossary and must not be read as effective repository coverage.

Partner alerts go directly to participating providers and are not shown in the repository Security tab; user alerts and push-protection bypass alerts are distinct. The shared alert fragment conditions partner alerts to FPT/GHEC.
A row marked isduplicate gains a token-version link in middleware/UI. It is not permission to discard that source occurrence or treat its capability fields as redundant.

The UI converts capability values through Boolean and its filters use truthiness. An absent optional literal field can therefore display No; preserve absence separately from an explicit false source cell.

The pinned Next.js page embeds SecretScanningTable with patterns loaded by middleware; its loader preserves parsed entries via structured cloning. The schema and typed-data fidelity are separate from current platform behavior.

The secret-scanning README describes a Liquid Markdown renderer and calls isPublic public-repository availability and hasPushProtection enabled. The pinned component labels Partner and expresses support, not target activation. This documentation discrepancy is resolved for matrix interpretation by the pinned page/component/middleware; no upstream code is changed.

The pinned secret-scanning product fragment distinguishes public repositories, organization-owned private/internal repositories with the security feature enabled, and user-owned managed/enterprise cases. Pattern flags alone do not prove entitlement or enrollment.

The built-in-query landing page describes Default and security-extended suite membership and conditionally introduces Autofix details. These are reference facts, not proof a repository runs the query or has applied a fix.
Default runs by default; choosing security-extended adds queries. Security-extended includes all Default queries plus lower-precision/severity queries and can produce more false positives.

Security-and-quality extends security-extended with maintainability/reliability queries and uses advanced setup. Custom suites also require advanced setup; suite definitions select queries through ordered YAML instructions.

Query tables describe the latest CodeQL Action/CLI release at the pinned snapshot. Initial GHES bundled versions may lack queries; administrator upgrade may change coverage. No installed target version is established by table membership.

The security table generator derives Default from code-scanning pack membership and Extended from security-extended membership; check/x icons represent included/not included, preserving both independently.
Autofix inclusion is derived from a private supported-query ID list for the language and CodeQL source. It represents supported queries, not a guarantee of successful remediation or an executed fix.

The pinned Autofix feature gate contains FPT/GHEC but no GHES and says Enterprise Server is unavailable. Raw query rows still carry Autofix column icons; a visible raw cell must retain the feature-context limit.

The generator reads query metadata IDs/names/CWE tags, excludes entries without CWEs, and derives help URLs from language plus query ID. The resulting security table is not an exhaustive inventory of all CodeQL metadata/metrics queries.

Queries with equal display names can have distinct help identities including high/critical URL suffixes, as the Actions table demonstrates. Actual severity metadata is unverified here. Preserve exact help links and language; do not deduplicate by query name alone.

CodeQL and code-scanning entitlement fragments distinguish public website repositories and organization-owned repositories with Code Security enabled, including plan/platform conditions. Table support does not establish target entitlement.

The CodeQL pipeline generates security and code-quality tables separately. This batch validates only security table claims; it does not certify code-quality tables or execute the pipeline/private package.

Ten language wrappers preserve language scope, product/version front matter, the shared suite-behavior/version caveats, and their own table inclusion. The ten references are not interchangeable language coverage.

findings.description: Legacy public/private-support field labels require authoritative Partner/User alert interpretation; source README conflicts with pinned rendering. No old claim bytes are rewritten.
Raw Liquid strings and absent optional keys must remain raw/absent; Boolean UI output is not a source cell.
Query membership and Autofix support do not prove installed GHES/CLI availability, effective feature access, detection completeness, or remediation.

unreviewed_dependencies.dependency: Published version renderer, full Liquid engine, runtime allVersions and product variable expansion
unreviewed_dependencies.effect: Exact effective rendering for a concrete target/page-version remains unverified. Gates/caveats are preserved, not executed.

unreviewed_dependencies.dependency: CodeQL query-help bodies, actual CodeQL bundles and private @github/cocofix supported-query list
unreviewed_dependencies.effect: No algorithmic query behavior, current query correctness, release-to-runtime parity, or generated pipeline reproduction is certified.

unreviewed_dependencies.dependency: Provider internal source APIs and live capabilities
unreviewed_dependencies.effect: Literal pinned-table validation only; no contemporary platform or partner response guarantee.
Review paraphrases/source SHA and spans do not grant publication rights for raw upstream bodies.
